userStories.title: Round-2 runtime evidence gate (spike)
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want a repaired and extended Grok interrupt/resume diagnostic run on the native hosts available in this environment, so that we prove (or block on) a production-observable safe interrupt boundary M, current-prompt retention, sub-second Stop settlement, and exact process-tree cleanup before any production code changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Commit 2fb341bd is cherry-picked, bringing ONLY packages/providers/src/grok/interrupt-resume-spike.ts, the spike:interrupt:grok script in packages/providers/package.json, and plans/reports/spike-260920-0243-grok-interrupt-resume.md (kept immutable); no PR #217 plan/PRD/progress files come over

Runner builds every invocation through buildGrokArgs() and buildSpawnCommand() (minimal direct-module helper export only, no barrel export); safety restrictions modelled as ordinary allowed_tools/denied_tools node options; auto-updater disabled via documented flag/env and recorded as the one deliberate difference; --sandbox workspace NOT used for contract evidence

Runner replaces interruptImmediately/interruptOnFirstText booleans with the typed trigger set (spawn, first-stdout-event, first-event:<type>, pid-file), separates the Stop request from the termination trigger, and supports legacy + owned-tree spawn modes (detached POSIX process group; recorded Windows tree primitive)

Prompt-retention checks are turn-specific: fresh=current marker; resumed=inherited+current markers; fork=source+fork markers with source still resuming without the fork marker; repeated interrupt=all retained markers; report records booleans only

Runner records spawn-to-request, request-to-boundary, request-to-signal, signal-to-exit, request-to-provider-settlement, exit code, escalation, expected vs reported session id, resume result, marker-retention booleans, and exact descendant fingerprints (not process names)

Scenario matrix B0-B9 (+W1 on Windows) executed on every native host available to the agent (this host is macOS — run it there for real); hosts that cannot be reached are recorded in the gate table as BLOCKED pending operator evidence — never fabricated, waived, or substituted by containers/WSL claims

At least 10 new + 10 resumed + 10 forked samples per passed host with Stop requested before M and termination deferred to M; EVERY request-to-settlement sample < 1000 ms (min/median/max reported per turn kind and host); any violation marks that host BLOCKED — no 30-second fallback, no percentile waiver

New round-2 report at plans/reports/spike-<timestamp>-grok-interrupt-resume-round-2.md contains exact Grok build/hash + current-stable check, host/Bun versions, command shape, chosen M (or BLOCKED verdict), resumed-turn policy decision, tree primitives, timing summary, and sanitized PASS/BLOCKED gate table
plan.md validation log filled ONLY from the final report; unmet or unavailable entries left as blockers, not guessed
If reachable, a concise issue #186 comment links the sanitized report and states the verdict

No credentials, prompts, markers, model text, session contents, home paths, raw stderr, or env values in any committed artifact; disposable repo removed in finally; only runner-created UUIDs cleaned up from the disposable cwd
cd packages/providers && bun run type-check, bun test src/grok/provider.test.ts, bun test src/grok/event-parser.test.ts, plus root bun run lint --max-warnings 0 and bun run format:check all pass
GROK_CAPABILITIES.interrupt remains false; no production provider, executor, capability, route, schema, or UI file is modified by this story
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase file: phase-01-unblock-evidence-gates-spike-round-2.md. Commit 2fb341bd is in the repo but NOT an ancestor of HEAD — cherry-pick it. Runner is intentionally outside the package test script (needs XAI_API_KEY, network, API spend); offline gates prove it compiles and changes no Grok behavior. Decision rules: Phase 2 may only begin when B0-B9 pass on native macOS+Linux and W1 on native Windows; if any rule fails keep plan status blocked and record the exact failed gate — do not pick a slower boundary, POSIX-only publication, prompt-loss caveat, or fresh-session fallback. One successful build = validated build, not a minimum version.

userStories.title: Grok provider stream-abort seam
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want GrokProvider to honor the optional per-turn interruptSignal with assigned session identity, a cause-aware bounded tree-termination state machine, and the exact grok_aborted result, so that a graceful operator Stop after the proven boundary M yields a resumable session while capability stays false.
acceptanceCriteria: ENTRY GATE honored: no production edit until every field in plan.md's validation log is filled from a PASS round-2 report (M, resumed-turn policy, tree primitives, measured graceful-exit bound, validated build). If mandatory host/prompt/fork/descendant/latency evidence is missing or failed, make NO production change and record the blocker in notes

buildGrokArgs() also returns the effective expected session identity; with interruptSignal: new turn gets --session-id <uuid>, non-fork resume gets only --resume <existing>, fork gets --resume <source> --fork-session --session-id <new-uuid>; without interruptSignal argv is byte-for-byte unchanged; non-persistent resume error preserved
Reported end.sessionId differing from expected id yields terminal grok_session_id_mismatch error result (opaque expected/reported ids logged) — never grok_aborted

Explicit per-call cause state machine implemented (running pre-M -> waiting-for-M -> interrupting; post-M Stop -> interrupting; waiting-for-M deadline -> grok_interrupt_unmaterialized; grace expiry/SIGKILL -> grok_interrupt_forced_kill; node Cancel -> existing Query aborted throw; natural end before interrupt ownership -> natural result; fault before ownership -> existing failure)

One fixed settlement budget starts when interruptSignal aborts: pre-M wait deadline = 1000 ms ceiling minus Phase-1 termination/drain margin; not configurable; success or explicit failure settles by the original request deadline
Node Cancel re-checked before binary resolution, before spawn, after listener registration, and at settlement; it wins Stop races and still throws Query aborted

Natural completion frozen once parser accepts a valid matching end (later Stop cannot relabel it or signal); post-ownership exit 130/143, broken pipe, or trailing partial JSON cannot relabel a proven graceful interrupt; pre-Stop protocol fault stays a fault

Owned-tree spawn mode requested only when interruptSignal is present; POSIX detached process group and Windows tree primitive encapsulated behind GrokProcess (provider never builds shell command strings); already-exited/not-found benign; one termination coordinator owns escalation; Cancel-only shutdown retains existing 5000 ms grace

Parser gains hasReachedInterruptBoundary() (exact Phase-1 predicate), hasEnded(), closeOutstandingTools(outcome='unknown') idempotent, buildInterruptedResult(sessionId, resumed) emitting the exact triple; closeOutstandingTools('interrupted') emits one missing-output tool_result per open tool before the abort result

Settlement order after drain: close tools once -> node Cancel throw -> fault/mismatch/unmaterialized/forced-kill genuine failure -> graceful interrupt abort result with expected id -> existing transport/protocol/nonzero handling -> normal buildResult()
buildInterruptedResult requires non-empty id, includes tokens/cost/usage only from authoritative terminal usage, omits errors, never embeds grok_incomplete_output

Listeners removed and deadline/grace timers cleared in finally on natural, interrupted, cancelled, failed, and early-consumer-return paths; cleanup awaits process/stderr without masking the primary outcome

P1-P6 parser tests and T1-T18 provider tests pass using a controllable fake process (pushable stdout, independent stdout/stderr/exit settlement, recorded tree signals) and fake timers — no multi-second real timers; usage-contract case proves no-`end` interrupt carries no usageBreakdown/cost/tokens
GROK_CAPABILITIES.interrupt remains false; no executor, registry, generated-docs, route, or UI change in this story
Focused gates pass: bun test event-parser/provider/usage-contract/registry suites, bun run type-check (providers), root lint --max-warnings 0, format:check
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase file: phase-02-grok-provider-stream-abort-seam.md. Anchors: provider.ts:24 GrokProcess, :31 GrokSpawnOptions, :83 buildSpawnCommand, :110 buildGrokArgs, :270/:354 existing Query aborted; event-parser.ts:97 closeOutstandingTools, :113 buildResult, :123 grok_incomplete_output, :136 getSessionId; types.ts:609 interruptSignal, :843-847 interrupt union. TDD order: (1) characterization tests against current behavior pass first, (2) parser P1-P6, (3) identity/argv + process wrapper T1-T4/T17, (4) state machine T5-T16/T18, (5) type comments only, (6) regression gates with capability false. Exit criteria: P1-P6 + T1-T18 pass without weakening existing assertions; no successful interrupt result without expected concrete id; no Stop path exceeds the fixed 1000 ms ceiling in deterministic tests.

userStories.title: Executor conformance: direct and AI loop
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want the provider-neutral terminal-result predicate to accept the exact grok_aborted subtype and conformance tests proving the real Phase-2 chunk sequence follows Story 2.6 on direct AI nodes and AI loops, so that Grok interrupts park, persist, and resume exactly like the other providers.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing interrupt-focused selection and the full workflows package test script run green BEFORE the predicate change

G0 added and passing before the predicate change: an exact grok_aborted result with NO operator-interrupt flag follows the existing SDK-error/node-failed path (node_failed, no idle state) — remains true after the change

Predicate change is the only production executor change: keep Claude terminalReason allowlist; provider-normalized branch requires the complete triple stopReason==='aborted' && isError===true && ABORT_ERROR_SUBTYPES.has(errorSubtype) with set {deepseek_aborted, grok_aborted}; stale comment at dag-executor.ts:~475 corrected; no provider id, prefix match, or exception-text branch; live operator-interrupt token remains mandatory at each caller

G1 direct node mid-tool with output_format: provider-emitted interrupted tool_result removes the open tool so exactly one tool_completed exists; one interrupted status; no re-ask or node_failed; queued guidance + new instruction preserve receipt order ('older guidance\n\nnew instruction'); next call uses same session id with forkSession:false; node completes

G2 AI loop mid-text: interrupt parks inside the current iteration without consuming it or validating partial output; Send now resumes the same id in the interrupted iteration's attempt scope; loop-completion check runs only after the redirected turn
G3 natural unmarked Grok result racing Stop stays natural (queued guidance auto-drains or node finishes under existing queue rule; no interrupted row)
G4 near-miss Grok result WITH operator flag (missing/wrong triple member) remains a genuine provider failure, never idle

Grok conformance fixture registers interrupt:'stream-abort' only inside the test block while the production constant stays false; fixture yields the actual Phase-2 sequence (optional tool -> interrupted tool_result -> exact abort result)

Existing Claude, DeepSeek, queue-only, AI-loop, and loop-group interrupt tests (incl. the namespaced loop-group body-node test) are unchanged and green; no second provider-specific loop-group copy added
Validation passes: bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts -t 'grok conformance' and -t 'interrupt', workflows bun run test, root bun run type-check and lint --max-warnings 0
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase file: phase-03-engine-conformance-direct-loop.md. isInterruptMarkedResult at dag-executor.ts:481-493, call sites :2746 (direct) and :6510 (AI loop). Namespaced loop-group body nodes reuse the direct path — already covered by the existing generic test. If fixtures reveal a shared executor defect, STOP and revise the plan rather than patching with a provider-name branch. No UI file changes — provider-neutral dock/transcript already owns the approved states.

userStories.title: Capability publication, docs, and closeout
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want the proven Grok interrupt behavior published — capability flipped last, generated matrix regenerated, guide section written, acceptance report mapped to evidence, sprint row closed, and PR opened — so that Story 2.6 ships only what Phases 1-3 proved.
acceptanceCriteria: ENTRY GATE verified before flipping: Phase-1 report PASS on native macOS, Linux, and Windows; validation log names M, exact build, host versions, tree primitives, latency samples, and grace; Phase-2 provider/parser suites passed with capability false; Phase-3 conformance + all existing interrupt tests pass; no unresolved spec/UX conflict. If any item is absent, do NOT flip the capability or mark the sprint row done
GROK_CAPABILITIES.interrupt changed from false to 'stream-abort' as the final runtime edit; registry.test.ts Grok assertion updated to interrupt:'stream-abort'
bun run generate:capability-matrix run and inspected — only the Grok Turn interrupt cell changes; never hand-edit provider-capabilities.md
Provider and workflow focused suites re-run AFTER the flip (executor now registers Grok steering handles in ordinary tests/runtime)

ai-assistants.md gains a concise Grok interrupt-and-redirect section under '## Grok Build' covering all 8 contract bullets: Stop ends only the current turn with node running + Send now same session; queued guidance precedes new guidance in receipt order; in-flight tool shown as ⚠ interrupted with written files not rolled back; interrupt-then-continue (not soft-inject); exact tested build + native platforms phrased as tested compatibility (no invented minimum version); how to check/update Grok (grok --version, grok update --stable); sub-second Stop ack with explicit failure on unmaterialized session/graceful-shutdown failure; forced kill or session-id mismatch is a genuine provider failure; no fabricated token/USD accounting on no-end interrupts. No internal markers, session paths, kill commands, unsupported-host caveats, or 30-second wait documented

plans/reports/acceptance-<timestamp>-issue-186-grok-interrupt.md created mapping every plan acceptance criterion to Phase-1 gates, P/T provider tests, G executor tests, generated matrix, and guide anchors; includes commit, Grok/Bun versions, three hosts, Phase-1 report link, same-id + current-prompt retention proof, min/median/max latency + descendant verdict per host, validation commands/results, operational boundaries, and rollback steps; no credentials/prompts/markers/model output/home paths/session contents

Nine-angle final review (product, architecture, contracts, security/reliability, performance, completeness, testing, operations/compatibility, maintainability) completed; verified findings fixed and affected gates re-run; unresolved evidence recorded as blocker, not waived

Full validation sequence passes: providers focused tests + type-check, workflows focused + bun run test, bun run generate:capability-matrix, bun run check:capability-matrix, bun run build:docs, bun run validate (never root bun test)

sprint-status.yaml: only 2-6-interrupt-and-redirect-a-running-grok-agent changed backlog -> done, changed LAST after acceptance report + review; lightweight generated-doc/status checks re-run after the edit

PR opened from this feature branch to develop using .github/pull_request_template.md with 'Closes #186' and links to both spike reports + acceptance report; PR #217 closed as superseded (or its closing keyword removed) after its diagnostic commit/report are preserved here
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase file: phase-04-capability-docs-closeout.md. No archon doctor change or version-floor constant — checkGrok() already reports version/auth. Capability is static and host-independent, so it cannot be platform-dependent. Closeout order is strict: acceptance report -> nine-angle review -> diff hygiene check -> sprint flip last -> PR. Rollback: capability false + regenerate matrix first, then revert predicate/docs, then dormant provider seam; no data rollback needed.
